root_cause: The hidden annual residue guard used /\\bjr\\b/ inside a JavaScript regex literal, which matches a literal backslash-b sequence instead of a word boundary. Once the visible yearly price became legitimate again, the old fallback check on € 49.950 disappeared and the test exposed this false negative.
prevention_rule: When matching class-name word boundaries in JavaScript regex literals, use \b rather than \\b. Hidden legacy `.jr` pricing markup must be rejected independently of whether the same numeric yearly price is valid in visible intentional billing controls.

evidence.outcome: Hidden `.jr` annual residue is rejected by class semantics while legitimate visible yearly billing remains accepted.
